mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a basic operation on a data structure?
mcq.e: Insertion, deletion, traversal, searching, sorting and merging are data-structure operations. Encryption is a security transformation.

mcq.q: Which data structure gives efficient searching, insertion and deletion together, trading extra table space for speed?
mcq.e: A hash table gives average O(1) search, insert and delete, a time-space trade-off.

mcq.q: Which pair of data structures are both non-linear?
mcq.e: Tree and graph branch, so they are non-linear. Array, stack, queue and linked list are linear.

mcq.q: Which structure is used when processing must be postponed until other conditions are fulfilled?
mcq.e: A stack (LIFO) defers work: the latest postponed item is handled first.

mcq.q: Which of the following can NEVER contain a cycle?
mcq.e: A tree is acyclic (n nodes, n-1 edges). Graphs, circular queues and circular lists can have cycles.

mcq.q: Which notation gives an asymptotically tight bound (both upper and lower)?
mcq.e: Theta is tight upper and lower bound; Big-O is only an upper bound and Omega a lower bound.

mcq.q: What is the order of f(x) = 4x^2 - 5x + 3?
mcq.e: Only the fastest-growing term survives and constants are dropped, giving O(x^2).

mcq.q: Which ordering of average-case running times is correct, fastest first?
o: Binary search < linear search < quick sort < selection sort
Linear search < binary search < quick sort < selection sort
Binary search < quick sort < linear search < selection sort
Quick sort < binary search < linear search < selection sort
mcq.e: Binary search is O(log n), linear search O(n), quick sort O(n log n), selection sort O(n^2).

mcq.q: Which recurrence describes the worst case of quicksort?
mcq.e: T(n) = T(n-1) + Cn gives O(n^2). T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 is binary search.

mcq.q: The repeated-squaring routine exponentiate() that halves the exponent each time runs in:
mcq.e: Halving the exponent at each step gives Theta(log n) multiplications.

mcq.q: A loop runs j = 1; while (j <= n) j = j * 2. How many comparisons of j with n are made?
mcq.e: j takes values 1, 2, 4 ... so the test succeeds log2 n + 1 times (counting the doubling steps as in the standard result).

mcq.q: Which problem is NOT computable by any algorithm?
mcq.e: The halting problem is undecidable; no algorithm exists for it.

mcq.q: Strassen's matrix multiplication has running time:
mcq.e: Strassen uses 7 multiplications, giving exponent log2 7, about n^2.81.

mcq.q: N insertions are required but only about sqrt(log N) other operations. Which structure is best?
mcq.e: An unsorted array inserts in O(1); the few other operations hardly matter.

mcq.q: How many elements does the array E[-4:1, 6:10] have?
In row-major order, array B[4][5] has base 5000 and element size 2. What is LOC(B[2][3])?
C[3][4][5] is stored row-major, base 3000, element size 1. What is LOC(C[2][3][4])?
In a tri-diagonal matrix stored row-wise in a 1-D array, where is element (i, j)?
mcq.e: Index = 2i + j - 2, and only 3n - 2 cells are needed.

mcq.q: Why does an array enjoy spatial locality?
o: It is stored in one contiguous memory block
mcq.e: Contiguous storage means touching one element brings its neighbours into the cache.

mcq.q: What is the time complexity of deleting the first element of an array of n elements?
mcq.e: The remaining n - 1 elements must shift, so deletion is O(n).

mcq.q: Which statement about a singly linked list is INCORRECT?
o: Its size can grow and shrink dynamically
It allows random and direct access to any element
The last node's pointer is NULL
mcq.e: Reaching an index costs O(n); random access is the false claim.

mcq.q: Inserting a new node at the head of a singly linked list takes:
mcq.e: Only the new node's next and the head pointer change.

mcq.q: How many pointers change when a node is inserted between two nodes of a doubly linked list?
mcq.e: The new node's two pointers plus one pointer in each neighbour make four; a singly list needs two.

mcq.q: A deque built on a singly linked list deletes at the rear in:
mcq.e: You must walk to the predecessor of the last node. A doubly linked list makes it O(1).

mcq.q: Which structure is used for round-robin CPU allocation?
mcq.e: The last node pointing back to the first suits cyclic allocation.

mcq.q: Which technique is NOT suitable on a linked list?
mcq.e: Binary search needs O(1) access to the middle element, which lists lack.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT an application of a stack?
mcq.e: Asynchronous transfer between processes is a queue/pipe job.

mcq.q: Popping from an empty stack causes:
mcq.e: Pop on empty = underflow; push on full = overflow.

mcq.q: What is the prefix form of A + B * C?
mcq.e: * binds tighter, so B*C becomes *BC and the prefix form is +A*BC.

mcq.q: Which prefix expression equals (A*B + C)/(E - F*G)?
o: / + * A B C - E * F G
/ * + A B C - E * F G
+ / * A B C - E * F G
/ + * A B C * - E F G
mcq.e: Numerator +*ABC, denominator -E*FG, joined by /.

mcq.q: Convert the prefix expression * + a b - c d to postfix.
mcq.e: (a+b) becomes ab+, (c-d) becomes cd-, then * last.

mcq.q: Which postfix string has the operator last in each sub-expression, e.g. a b c * + d e - + ?
mcq.e: In postfix the operator follows its operands, so no brackets or precedence are needed.

mcq.q: While evaluating postfix 3 2 + 7 * 6 5 + 4 * -, what is on top of the stack just before the second +?
mcq.e: After 3 2 + 7 * the stack holds 35, then 6 and 5 are pushed, so 5 is on top.

mcq.q: In a linear queue, where does insertion take place?
mcq.e: Queues are FIFO: insert at the rear, delete at the front.

mcq.q: A circular queue (ring buffer) is used mainly to:
mcq.e: It reuses freed front slots, curing false overflow of a linear queue.

mcq.q: In a circular queue of size MAX, the queue is full when:
mcq.e: Full is (rear+1) mod MAX = front; front = rear = -1 means empty.

mcq.q: Which structure is best used to implement a priority queue?
mcq.e: A binary heap gives O(log n) insert and extract.

mcq.q: Insertion into a linked queue with new node PTR is done by:
mcq.e: Link after the old rear, then move REAR. FRONT is never touched.

mcq.q: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height n (root at level 0)?
mcq.e: A complete tree of height n has 2^(n+1) - 1 nodes; the minimum is n + 1.

mcq.q: A full binary tree has n leaves. How many degree-2 nodes does it have?
mcq.e: In such a tree, leaves minus one equals the number of degree-2 nodes.

mcq.q: A binary tree with n nodes has how many NULL pointers?
mcq.e: n+1 null pointers; a threaded tree reuses them as threads.

mcq.q: How many different BSTs can be formed from 4 keys?
mcq.e: The Catalan number for 4 keys is 14.

mcq.q: Which traversal order is Left, Right, Node?
mcq.e: Pre = NLR, In = LNR, Post = LRN.

mcq.q: The preorder traversal of a binary tree is 38,14,8,23,18,20,56,45,82,70 (BST). What is its postorder?
mcq.e: Rebuilding the BST gives left subtree rooted at 14 and right at 56; postorder is 8,20,18,23,14,45,70,82,56,38.

mcq.q: In a BST, in-order traversal produces:
mcq.e: Left < node < right, so in-order visits keys in ascending order.

mcq.q: When deleting a BST node with two children, it is replaced by its:
mcq.e: The inorder successor is correct; preorder is the false claim.

mcq.q: Inorder of a tree is QSPTRU and preorder is PQSRTU. What is its postorder?
mcq.e: P is the root; Q,S on the left and R,T,U on the right give S,Q,T,U,R,P.

mcq.q: In an AVL tree, a node needs rebalancing when its balance factor becomes:
mcq.e: Allowed values are -1, 0, +1; reaching +/-2 triggers rotation.

mcq.q: Which AVL rotations are double rotations?
mcq.e: LL and RR are single rotations; LR and RL are double.

mcq.q: Which statement about B-trees is false?
o: It is not a binary tree
It is widely used for external memory
All leaves are at the same level
Leaves may be at different levels
mcq.e: All leaves of a B-tree are at the same level; the opposite claim is false.

mcq.q: In a red-black tree, newly inserted non-root nodes are coloured:
mcq.e: A new root is black and a non-root insertion is red.

mcq.q: In a 1-based array heap, the parent of the node at index i is:
mcq.e: Parent = floor(i/2); children are 2i and 2i+1.

mcq.q: A vertex of degree 1 is called:
mcq.e: Pendant = degree 1; an isolated vertex has degree 0.

mcq.q: A simple graph has 8 vertices. What is the maximum number of edges?
Which data structure does BFS use?
mcq.e: BFS uses a queue and DFS a stack.

mcq.q: A spanning tree of a connected graph with n vertices has how many edges?
mcq.e: Exactly n - 1 edges; n/2 is invalid.

mcq.q: Which problem is NOT NP-complete?
mcq.e: Shortest path is solved in polynomial time by Dijkstra.

mcq.q: Binary search is unsuccessful when:
mcq.e: End < Beg means the range is empty.

mcq.q: What is the maximum number of comparisons binary search needs on 12,000 sorted elements?
Which of the following is NOT a hash function method?
mcq.e: Division, mid-square and folding are hash functions; probing resolves collisions.

mcq.q: Using h(k) = k mod 57, what is h(197)?
Which is NOT a collision-resolution technique?
mcq.e: Folding is a hash function, not a collision technique.

mcq.q: Keys 22, 28, 23, 12, 13 are inserted by h(k)=k mod 9 with linear probing in a table of size 9. Where does 13 go?
mcq.e: 13 hashes to 4 (22 there), 5 holds 23, so 13 goes to 6.

mcq.q: Worst-case comparisons of bubble sort on 15 elements are:
Which sorting algorithm is NOT stable?
mcq.e: Heap, quick and selection sort are unstable.

mcq.q: Which pair of sorts is recursive divide and conquer?
mcq.e: Quick and merge sort divide and recurse; bubble and insertion are iterative.

mcq.q: The worst case of quicksort is:
mcq.e: Sorted input with an extreme pivot gives Theta(n^2); a median pivot restores O(n log n).

mcq.q: Which sort is O(n log n) in every case and best suited for linked lists?
mcq.e: Merge sort needs only sequential access.

mcq.q: Which sort needs at most n - 1 swaps but is O(n^2) in both best and worst case?
mcq.e: Selection sort always scans for the minimum, with few swaps.

mcq.q: Which of the following is solved by dynamic programming and NOT divide and conquer?
mcq.e: Floyd-Warshall is DP.

mcq.q: Which statement about greedy algorithms is FALSE?
o: They consider one input at a time
mcq.e: Greedy does not examine all feasible solutions.

mcq.q: Dynamic programming is suited to problems with:
mcq.e: DP relies on overlapping subproblems.

mcq.q: Which is solved by backtracking?
mcq.e: Subset-sum and n-queens use trial with undo.

tf.s: A hash table has average O(1) search, insert and delete.
Big-O gives a lower bound on running time.
tf.n: Big-O is the upper bound; Omega is the lower bound.

tf.s: Intractable problems are solved in polynomial time.
Linked lists support random access in O(1).
Evaluating a prefix expression uses a stack scanned right to left.
Symbol balancing is a queue application.
In a BST the right subtree holds greater values.
Deleting a two-child BST node uses its preorder successor.
DFS uses less memory than BFS.
tf.n: It stores one path, not a frontier.

tf.s: Binary search can be applied to a linked list efficiently.
tf.n: No O(1) access to the middle.

tf.s: Floyd-Warshall is a divide and conquer algorithm.
The handshaking lemma says the degree sum equals twice the number of edges.
The best case of binary search is O(log n).
tf.n: The best case is one comparison.

The structure used to implement DFS is a ______.
Binary heap is used to implement a ______ queue.
Row-major address of A[i][j] is B + w x (i x C + j), where C is the number of ______.
The balance factor of an AVL node must lie in {-1, 0, ______}.
The sorting algorithm with n(n-1)/2 worst-case comparisons, repeatedly swapping adjacent elements, is ______ sort.
A degree-1 vertex in a graph is called a ______ vertex.
In division hashing, h(k) = k ______ m.
